title: While We’re Here
subtitle: Small essays on attention, time, and being alive
author: Adam Hickey
backCoverLine: You can walk around a familiar lake believing almost nothing is happening, while simultaneously moving through thousands of invisible systems.
backCoverBlurb: Essays on attention, on order that arrives with nobody holding a plan, on living inside a change while its rules are still unsettled, and on the ordinary shared days that turn out to be the whole thing. Four of them, meant to be read in order — each about the length of a walk.

sequence.note: Before a book becomes an object in the world, it is something one person makes and hands to another.

entries.title: To the Love of My Life
entries.by: Made by Fabiola. One copy, for one reader.

entries.title: Misery Is…
entries.by: Written and bound by the author as a child, and kept. Inside, in pencil: “Misery is when your mom embarrass younn front of your friends.”

dedication: For my parents, who taught me to look, and for Fabiola, who looks with me
$comment_blurb: Rewritten 25 Aug 2026 for the four-essay edition. The old blurb ended “A book for reading straight through, or for opening at random on a Tuesday”, and the second half of that stopped being true: eight essays of eleven hundred words invite dipping, four of eighteen hundred do not. A back cover that promises a reading experience the book no longer offers is the same class of fault as a credit for an image that was cut. “Nobody holding a plan” echoes Part II’s title; “the length of a walk” is honest about the new length and is the book’s own recurring measure.
